correctness.rationale: Direct Ore evaluation in the order-two Frobenius extension gives t^n+a t^m u+1=0 for n odd and t^{2m}+a t^m+1=0 for n even. Unique root recovery and norm consistency reduce odd n to inversion orbits in the n-th power subgroup; even n to inversion orbits in the (n/2)-power subgroup. All boundary cases including a=0, -1 subgroup membership, and degenerate subgroup size are proven. Exact independent recurrence checker passes 100 prime quadratic-extension cases and 918720 evaluations; computations are support, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Right linear-factor counts are a natural finer invariant for the newly enumerated sparse Ore trinomial family. This is the complete coefficient-resolved classification for all positive n and every odd prime power q over degree-two extensions, with a surprising even/odd exponent bifurcation, exact support sizes and a sharp incidence law. Unlike a single parameter example or a direct renaming, the theorem resolves a whole naturally varying family; it does not purport to count higher-degree factors.
